questions.prompt: When do you need to enter your UPI PIN?

options.text: Only when you are sending money
To receive money from a buyer
options.explanationWrong: A UPI PIN is never needed to receive money. Anyone who says it is, is trying to trick you.

options.text: To read a message from your bank
options.explanationWrong: Reading a message never needs your PIN. Be careful with any message that asks for it.
Being polite does not make a request safe. Your PIN is private, always.

questions.explanationCorrect: Your UPI PIN is only for sending money. You never need it to receive money.

questions.prompt: A buyer says: 'Enter your PIN to receive the payment.' What should you do?

options.text: Enter the PIN quickly so the buyer does not leave
options.explanationWrong: Rushing is what the scammer wants. Entering the PIN would send money out.

options.text: Enter the PIN, but only the first two digits
options.explanationWrong: Any part of your PIN is a secret. Do not enter it at all.

options.text: Do not enter it. Decline the request and report the sender
Send the PIN in a chat so the buyer can do it for you
options.explanationWrong: Never share your PIN with anyone, for any reason.

questions.explanationCorrect: Decline, do not enter your PIN, and block and report the sender. Receiving money never needs your PIN.

questions.prompt: What happens when you approve a collect request?

options.explanationWrong: It is the other way round. A collect request asks you to pay.

options.text: Nothing, it only confirms your name
options.explanationWrong: Approving is a real action. In real life it can lead to a payment.
Approving a request has nothing to do with hiding your balance.

questions.explanationCorrect: A collect request asks you to pay. Approving it, and entering your PIN, sends money out of your account.
